note: The zip central directory stores the entry filename length in a 16-bit field; this attacker-controlled value (up to 65535) is parsed from the input zip file and later reported to the caller as fileInfo.size_filename.
The full untrusted filename length is forwarded to the field copier, which truncates the copy to the caller-provided buffer size but never reports that truncation.
Fixed 256-byte stack buffer (FileNameSize == 256) that will hold the zip entry filename.

code: if (unzGetCurrentFileInfo(m_ZipFileHandle, &fileInfo, filename, FileNameSize, nullptr, 0, nullptr, 0) == UNZ_OK) {
note: unzGetCurrentFileInfo fills at most FileNameSize bytes into the 256-byte buffer, but fileInfo.size_filename still holds the full attacker-controlled filename length from the zip.

Root cause: no check that fileInfo.size_filename fits the 256-byte buffer. The std::string constructor is given the untrusted full length as the byte count, so it reads far past the end of the undersized stack buffer.

Sink: for a filename longer than 256 characters (fileInfo.size_filename > FileNameSize), the string constructor performs an out-of-bounds read of fileInfo.size_filename bytes starting from the 256-byte stack buffer, overflowing the stack buffer (stack-based buffer overflow).
